profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting in an ML research lab evaluating a proposal to build a prototype 'Deep Arbitrary Polynomial Chaos Neural Network' (DAPC-NN) for surrogate modeling of stochastic PDE outputs. The team already agrees on the broad idea—replace standard affine neuron pre-activations with data-driven orthonormal polynomial feature blocks derived from hidden activations—but this review is to judge whether the current implementation plan is actually ready for a 6-week internal benchmark. The agenda is to review the proposed node-level basis construction, the meaning of 'orthonormal' in the design, the planned validation package, and what counts as sufficient design sign-off before engineering starts. The expected outcome is a conditional approval of the design with a short list of modifications, although each participant silently assumes different boundaries for what that approval covers.

members.name: Dr. Elena Markovic
members.expertise: uncertainty quantification, polynomial chaos expansions, scientific machine learning
members.background: Elena leads the lab's probabilistic modeling track and previously worked on adaptive arbitrary polynomial chaos methods for reduced-order models in computational physics.
members.private_state: She wants the proposal approved quickly so the group can claim a novel architecture before a competing lab publishes something similar, but she is worried that too much implementation detail will delay the benchmark kickoff.
hidden_assumptions: If a basis is described as orthonormal at a layer, that orthonormality is with respect to the empirical activation distribution on the training split used to fit the basis.
A design review sign-off means the mathematical architecture and validation philosophy are settled; exact engineering safeguards can be filled in during implementation.
The 'degree-3 block' in the prototype means keeping all homogeneous polynomial terms up to total degree 3 after pruning near-collinear moments, not necessarily every combinatorial term.
When the plan says to compare against the baseline network, the intended baseline is the current lab MLP benchmark with the same parameter budget and standard per-seed averaging.

Stability checks are satisfied if the basis construction remains numerically well-conditioned on the main benchmark distributions the paper targets, even if rare OOD activation drift is not explicitly tested yet.

members.name: Ravi Iyer
members.expertise: deep learning systems, experiment infrastructure, numerical linear algebra
members.background: Ravi builds reproducible training pipelines for the lab's scientific ML projects and has recently been handling architecture reviews that need to transition into production-grade experiment code.
members.private_state: He wants the design to be concrete enough that his team can implement it without revisiting core assumptions later, and he is especially concerned about silent failure modes in basis generation and evaluation reporting.
hidden_assumptions: If a basis is called orthonormal in the design, it should remain approximately orthonormal under the streamed training distribution after augmentation and batching, not only on a one-time fitting sample.
A design review sign-off means the implementation contract is stable enough that engineering should not need to infer missing scope around logging, ablations, and failure handling.
A 'degree-3 block' means the full set of polynomial interactions through total degree 3 for each node input group, because otherwise parameter counts and kernel generation logic are ambiguous.

When someone says baseline comparison, the natural reference is the reproducible benchmark suite that includes the tuned ResMLP variant, calibration plots, and per-case breakdowns required by the lab's current review template.

Stability has to include behavior under activation distribution shift across seeds, curriculum stages, and normalization settings, because those are routine execution conditions rather than optional stress tests.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the polynomial basis should be 'orthonormal at each node.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means orthonormal with respect to the empirical measure induced by hidden activations on the training split used during basis fitting, which is enough to justify the theoretical framing and initial experiments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means orthonormality should hold approximately throughout training under the effective streamed distribution after batching, augmentation, and normalization changes, because otherwise the implementation will violate the stated design property in practice.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds mathematically precise, so both assume the other shares the standard interpretation; neither expects that the other is applying a different operational standard for when the property 'counts.'

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they just need enough for 'design sign-off' today.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes sign-off covers architectural correctness, key equations, and a minimal validation plan, leaving instrumentation details, fallback logic, and some ablation mechanics for implementation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes sign-off should also lock down experiment logging, basis-regeneration triggers, failure criteria, and exact review outputs so engineering does not make latent research decisions later.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research settings, 'sign-off' often sounds like a routine milestone, and both are cooperative; they each assume their own boundary is the obvious one for a design review.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the proposal should beat 'the baseline suite.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the older internal UQ benchmark package centered on the lab's standard MLP surrogate with matched parameter count and seed-averaged RMSE.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the newer reproducibility suite used in recent reviews, which includes the tuned ResMLP baseline, calibration diagnostics, and stratified error tables.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The lab informally uses the same phrase for two nearby benchmark bundles, and both people have recently worked with different versions; because they overlap substantially, surface agreement feels safe.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both endorse implementing a 'degree-3 block' for the prototype.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a sparse, moment-pruned construction that keeps homogeneous terms through degree 3 only when the empirical Gram procedure indicates they are informative and numerically stable.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects deterministic generation of the full interaction set through total degree 3 before any later optimization pass, because that is the straightforward way to define shapes, caching, and reproducibility.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They appear aligned on the headline choice of degree, and the implementation detail hides behind a shared technical phrase; each assumes the generation method is standard from their own perspective.
